text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, visiting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Ramallah, affirms the centrality of the Palestinian cause in Jordanian affairs.

- Coordinating committee of opposition parties delay their regular Monday meeting to await decision from Islamic Action Front on participation in November elections. Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says contacts continue with Islamist leaders. Labour unions say their members won't boycott.
- Cabinet agrees to finance a dam on Mujib river with a 35 million cubic metre capacity with 52 million dinars ($73 million) of debt owed by Yugoslavia from its purchases of Jordanian phosphate.
- Jordan to repay 13 million markka of debt to Finland in the form of phosphate exports, with the remainder of the 22 million markka debt forgiven under Paris Club agreement.

- Cairo Amman Bank says will meet Central Bank requirements to raise capital to 20 million dinars by end of the year. Says it aiming for 25 million dinars but could reach as high as 30 million if profits are good.
- Interior Minister says government has had meetings with Islamist figures.
- Hussein Majalli, defence lawyer for soldier who shot dead Israeli girls, says the sentence can be approved, appealed or annulled by the army chief of staff.
- Majali renews Jordanian support for Palestinian leadership and people.
- Palestinian airlines to start flights to Jordan on Wednesday.
- Cairo Amman Bank reports 7.3 million dinar net profits in 1996.
- Jordan Insurance company reports 1.5 million dinar profit in financial year to March 1997.
- Former Prime Minister Ahmed Obeidat expresses shock at soldier's severe sentence for shooting Israelis.
